title: Throughly charmed by A Walk On The Moon Between the incredible cast, ...
transcript: I was fully expecting to walk out of A walk on the moon going, that was nice. But instead I was thoroughly charmed by this lovely little musical based on a 90s movie I've never seen. A walk on the moon takes place at a Jewish bungalow colony in the summer of 1969, where Pearl, a stay at home mother, begins to wonder if the life she's built is the only life she'll ever have. Which leads to an unexpected summer romance which changes everything. Now, this is a story we've seen before, the bridges of Madison County, waitress, the Baker's Wife. Many of my favourite musicals, actually. But it is this cast which elevates the story to the next level. Like the women who surround Pearl and bring so much humour and warmth to her community. Shout out to Megan Kane and Becca Suskauer, who I just adore watching on stage. And Sophie Palermo, who plays Pearl's teenage daughter, spends the musical chasing her dreams and making Pearl realize she never got a chance to chase hers. Andrea Burns is her mother in law and is just a delight. Sam Gravat, who plays the most charming, free spirited Jack Kerouac. I get it, girl. Max Turner, who should be a completely forgettable, boring, devoted husband, but Max makes him feel fully realised and you find yourself kind of rooting for him. And of course, the heart of this piece, Talia Sussauer. She brings so much yearning and vulnerability to Pearl. You feel everything that she's wrestling with and every desire that she has. And it means that even when Pearl is making mistakes, you can't help but empathise with her. And of course, Talia's voice is absolutely stunning. Anyway, A walk on the moon surprised me in the best way. It's the perfect summer musical. It made me want to run away to the Catskills. And it's playing until August 22nd at the Laura Pells Theatre. I'm definitely coming back later this summer because I have to bring my mom.
